chunks: Al-Fadl, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from some of the companions of Abu Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

Regarding the daughters of a sister and a grandfather, he said: 'For the daughters of the sister is one-third, and what remains is for the grandfather. So he established the daughters of the sister in the place of the sister, and made the grandfather at the status of the brother.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status of / in the place of

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a grandfather when competing with the daughters of a sister?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'ta'sib' (residuary inheritance) by establishing a functional equivalence between siblings and their descendants in the absence of closer male heirs. The Imam demonstrates that the daughters of a sister are treated as sisters, and the grandfather as a brother, thereby securing the grandfather's share as a residuary heir after the fixed portion of the nieces is allocated. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach of aligning inheritance dynamics with the structural logic of the Quranic shares while accommodating specific familial configurations.
